system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Detection-branch veto: MVFA's image-label-trained detection maps filter pseudo-masks for the segmentation branch
SUMMARY: Use MVFA's own detection branch, which is trained with reliable image-level labels on all six source datasets, to keep only those pseudo-mask patches that the detection branch also considers anomalous, and train the segmentation branch on the agreed patches.
HYPOTHESIS: Restricting segmentation-branch targets to patches where the label-restricted pseudo-mask and the top-20% patches of the detection branch's map agree raises pseudo-mask precision by at least 15 points at a recall loss below 10 points, and MVFA trained this way recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
RATIONALE: The inspiring idea trains only on confident pseudo-labels. By analogy with co-training and co-teaching, where two views of the data filter each other's noisy labels, MVFA already contains a second view: the detection adapters are trained with an image-level BCE on mean-pooled patch maps for every source image (verified in train_zero.py), so their patch maps learn where image-level evidence comes from, using reliable labels and all six datasets. Agreement between this weakly supervised view and the feature-distance pseudo-masks is a confidence signal internal to the target method, needing no external model; disagreeing patches are ignored rather than relabelled. This uses MVFA's two-branch architecture as a self-checking mechanism, which none of the cited works do.
METHOD: 1) Stage 1: train MVFA's det branch only (train_zero.py with seg loss disabled) on all six sources for 20 epochs, selected on source validation image AUROC. 2) Detection patch map D(p) per abnormal source training image (level-averaged, as MVFA computes it). 3) Label-restricted pseudo-mask M(p) from frozen CLIP features. 4) Targets: positive where M(p) = 1 and D(p) in the image's top 20%; negative where M(p) = 0 and D(p) below the image median; ignore otherwise; normal images all negative. 5) Stage 2: train both branches as in MVFA (det branch continues from stage 1), seg loss = masked Focal + Dice over non-ignored pixels. 6) Agreement quantile (top 10/20/30%) selected on source validation. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; pseudo-masks alone; detection map alone as targets; agreement targets. Masks removed from all 3 masked sources, and the image-only datasets added as pseudo-mask sources. Metrics: pseudo-mask precision/recall vs true masks, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if agreement does not raise precision by 15 points or the trained model does not outperform both single-view targets.

Idea B:
TITLE: Detection-gated mean teacher: online pseudo-mask refinement accepted only where MVFA's detection branch agrees
SUMMARY: Refine pseudo-masks online with an EMA teacher of the segmentation adapters, but accept the teacher's updates only on patches where the image-label-trained detection branch agrees, ignoring the rest.
HYPOTHESIS: Gating mean-teacher updates by detection-branch agreement yields pseudo-mask precision at least 10 points higher than the ungated mean teacher at equal recall, and the final model recovers at least 92% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities in a single training run.
RATIONALE: The veto parent filters a fixed pseudo-mask with the detection branch; the mean-teacher parent improves targets online but can drift toward its own errors. Combining them, the detection branch, trained on reliable image labels for all six sources, acts as a gate on every teacher update: targets change only where an independent view supports the change. This keeps the mean teacher's progressive improvement and the veto's precision, inside one training run and using only MVFA's two existing branches.
METHOD: 1) Initial targets y0: label-restricted rule. 2) Detection branch trained jointly from the start (BCE on mean-pooled det map, as in MVFA); its patch map D_t is read from the current model. 3) Teacher: EMA of seg_adapters (decay 0.99). 4) From epoch 10, per epoch and abnormal image: proposed target y' = (1 - alpha_t) y0 + alpha_t q_teacher; accept y' at patches where D_t is in the image's top 20% (if y' > 0.5) or below its median (if y' < 0.5); elsewhere keep the previous target; pixels with no agreement are ignored. alpha_t ramps 0 to 0.5 by epoch 30. 5) Loss: masked Focal + soft Dice. Hyper-parameters as MVFA otherwise; gate quantiles selected on source validation.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; static pseudo-masks; veto only; mean teacher only; gated mean teacher. Metrics: pseudo-mask precision/recall over epochs, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if gating does not raise precision by 10 points or if the gated model is not better than both parents.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>

CONFIDENCE: LOW
WINNER=A
